name: Wall push-up

technique.setup: Stand an arm's length from a wall and place the hands on it at chest height, slightly wider than the shoulders. Step the feet back until the body leans in one straight line from head to heels.
cues: Squeeze the glutes and keep the ribs down
Keep the elbows about 45 degrees from the body
Lower until the nose nearly touches the wall
Push the wall away at the top
mistakes: Hips sagging or sticking out behind
Elbows flared straight out to the sides
Only bending the elbows a little instead of using the full range
stopIf: Sharp or joint pain in the wrist, elbow or shoulder
Pinching at the front of the shoulder

media.searchHint: Calisthenicmovement wall push up beginner tutorial

notes: Starting point if knee or incline push-ups are not yet possible with good form.

name: Incline push-up

technique.setup: Place the hands on a sturdy raised surface (kitchen counter, table, box or bench), slightly wider than the shoulders. Walk the feet back until the body is one straight line from head to heels; the higher the surface, the easier the rep.
cues: Squeeze the glutes and keep the ribs down
Keep the elbows about 45 degrees from the body
Lower the chest all the way to the edge
Push the surface away at the top
mistakes: Hips sagging or piking up
Elbows flared straight out to the sides
Half reps that stop well above the edge
stopIf: Sharp or joint pain in the wrist, elbow or shoulder
Pinching at the front of the shoulder
The surface slides or wobbles

notes: Log the surface height; lower it as reps get easy. Marchon press-up progression starts here.

technique.setup: Kneel on a mat with the hands under the shoulders, slightly wider, fingers spread. Walk the hands forward until the body is one straight line from head to knees.
cues: Squeeze the glutes so the hips stay in line
Keep the elbows about 45 degrees from the body
Lower the chest to a fist's height from the floor
Push the floor away at the top
mistakes: Bending at the hips so only the arms move
Elbows flared straight out to the sides
Half reps that stop well above the floor
stopIf: Sharp or joint pain in the wrist, elbow or shoulder
Pinching at the front of the shoulder
Kneecap pain (add more padding or switch to incline)

media.searchHint: Hybrid Calisthenics knee push up proper form beginner

name: Full push-up

technique.setup: Hands under the shoulders, slightly wider, fingers spread. Legs straight, feet together, body in one straight line from head to heels.
cues: Squeeze the glutes and keep the ribs down
Keep the elbows about 45 degrees from the body
Lower the chest to a fist's height from the floor
Push the floor away at the top
mistakes: Hips sagging or piking up
Elbows flared straight out to the sides
Half reps that stop well above the floor
Head dropping forward first
stopIf: Sharp or joint pain in the wrist, elbow or shoulder
Pinching at the front of the shoulder

notes: Journal doses were 12-15 x3; start at 3x5 and build to 3x8 before moving on.

name: Diamond push-up

technique.setup: From a full push-up position, bring the hands close together under the chest (thumbs and index fingers can form a diamond, or keep hands just inside shoulder width if that pinches). Body in one straight line from head to heels.
cues: Squeeze the glutes and keep the ribs down
Keep the elbows tucked close to the ribs
Lower the chest to the hands
Push the floor away at the top
mistakes: Elbows flaring out wide
Hips sagging as the arms tire
Half reps that stop well above the hands
stopIf: Sharp or joint pain in the wrist, elbow or shoulder
Pain at the back or point of the elbow

notes: Journal used close grip inside WNC push-up clusters.

name: Archer push-up

technique.setup: Set up in a push-up with the hands about twice shoulder width, fingers turned slightly out. Body in one straight line from head to heels.
cues: Shift toward one hand and bend that elbow
Keep the other arm long and nearly straight
Keep the hips square and level to the floor
Push back to the middle before switching sides
mistakes: Twisting the hips toward the working side
Bending both arms equally so it becomes a wide push-up
Shoulder shrugging up to the ear on the working side
stopIf: Sharp or joint pain in the wrist, elbow or shoulder
Pinching at the front of the shoulder

media.searchHint: FitnessFAQs archer push up tutorial progression

notes: Journal dose was 8x4 or 8-10 x3, with normal push-ups as the fallback.

name: Pseudo-planche push-up

technique.setup: Do wrist prep first. Set up in a push-up with the fingers turned out and the hands beside the lower ribs, then lean the shoulders forward past the hands.
cues: Keep the lean the whole rep
Round the upper back slightly and push the floor away
Squeeze the glutes and keep the ribs down
Tuck the elbows to the ribs as you lower
mistakes: Losing the forward lean as the chest goes down
Hips sagging into a banana shape
Leaning further than the wrists can tolerate
stopIf: Sharp or joint pain in the wrist, elbow or shoulder
Pain at the inside of the elbow or the bicep tendon
Wrist pain that lingers after the set

media.searchHint: FitnessFAQs pseudo planche push up tutorial

notes: Bent-arm, so not straight_arm, but it loads the wrists heavily. Journal dose was 6-8 x3.

name: Fist push-up

technique.setup: Make fists and place them on a folded mat under the shoulders, knuckles down and thumbs facing forward, wrists straight. Use the knees if full push-ups are not yet possible.
cues: Keep the wrists straight, in line with the forearms
Squeeze the glutes and keep the ribs down
Keep the elbows about 45 degrees from the body
Push the floor away at the top
mistakes: Wrists bending to the side on the knuckles
Doing it on a hard floor without padding
Hips sagging or piking up
stopIf: Sharp or joint pain in the wrist, elbow or shoulder
Knuckle pain
Any wrist pain at all (it should be pain-free with a wrist niggle)

media.searchHint: knuckle push up wrist pain alternative Antranik

notes: Wrist-niggle alternate for palm-loaded pushing: neutral wrist, no extension. Can be done from the knees.

name: Dumbbell-handle push-up

technique.setup: Place two hex dumbbells (they must not roll) under the shoulders, handles parallel to the body, and grip them with straight wrists. Body in one straight line from head to heels, or on the knees.
cues: Keep the wrists straight, in line with the forearms
Squeeze the glutes and keep the ribs down
Keep the elbows tucked about 45 degrees
Lower the chest between the handles
mistakes: Using round dumbbells that can roll
Sinking the shoulders far below the handles at the bottom
Hips sagging or piking up
stopIf: Sharp or joint pain in the wrist, elbow or shoulder
Pinching at the front of the shoulder
A dumbbell shifts or rolls

media.searchHint: push up on dumbbells neutral grip wrist friendly form

notes: Wrist-niggle alternate for palm-loaded pushing: neutral wrist, no extension. Stay within a normal push-up depth.

name: TRX push-up

technique.setup: Set the straps to mid-calf, hold the handles under the shoulders and walk the feet back. The more upright the body, the easier; log the angle.
cues: Keep the handles still and close to the body
Squeeze the glutes and keep the ribs down
Lower slowly for 3 seconds with elbows at about 45 degrees
Press up and squeeze the handles together
mistakes: Handles drifting wide apart
Hips sagging
Going so deep the shoulders roll forward
stopIf: Sharp or joint pain in the wrist, elbow or shoulder
Pinching at the front of the shoulder

notes: Journal used ring push-ups, slow 3 s down, 8-12 x4.

name: Band chest press

technique.setup: Anchor the band in a door at chest height and face away from it with one foot forward. Hold the handles at chest level with the elbows about 45 degrees from the body.
cues: Brace the core and keep the ribs down
Press the hands forward until the arms are straight
Keep the shoulders down away from the ears
Return slowly to chest level
mistakes: Leaning forward to make it easier
Shrugging the shoulders up
Letting the band snap the hands back
stopIf: Sharp or joint pain in the shoulder or elbow
Pinching at the front of the shoulder
A band that is frayed or a door that is not shut

media.searchHint: resistance band chest press door anchor form

notes: Wrist-niggle option for pushing at home: wrists stay neutral. Use a heavier band when 3x15 is easy.

name: Bench dip

technique.setup: Sit on the edge of a bench, hands beside the hips with fingers forward, and slide the hips just off the edge. Keep the knees bent and feet flat for the easiest version.
cues: Keep the shoulders down and the chest open
Lower until the elbows reach about 90 degrees, no deeper
Keep the hips close to the bench
Press up until the arms are straight
mistakes: Dropping far below 90 degrees
Shoulders rolling forward and shrugging up
Hips drifting far away from the bench
stopIf: Sharp or joint pain in the wrist, elbow or shoulder
Pinching or pain at the front of the shoulder

notes: Journal dose was 12x4 and 12-15 in supersets. Straighten the legs only once bent-knee reps are easy.

technique.setup: Stand on a box between the bars, grip them at the hip, and press up to straight arms. Step back down to the box at the end of the hold.
cues: Push the bars down and keep the shoulders down
Lock the elbows and keep the chest proud
Squeeze the legs together and the glutes
mistakes: Sinking into the shoulders so the neck disappears
Bent elbows that slowly give way
Swinging the legs
stopIf: Sharp or joint pain in the wrist, elbow or shoulder
Pinching at the front of the shoulder

name: Band-assisted dip

technique.setup: Loop a band across the two bars, stand on a box and kneel or step into the band, then press up to straight arms. Finish each set by stepping back onto the box.
cues: Keep the shoulders down away from the ears
Lean slightly forward and lower until the elbows reach about 90 degrees
Keep the elbows pointing back, not out
Press up to straight arms
mistakes: Dropping below 90 degrees and feeling a stretch at the front of the shoulder
Shrugging the shoulders up at the bottom
Bouncing out of the bottom using the band
stopIf: Sharp or joint pain in the wrist, elbow or shoulder
Pinching or pain at the front of the shoulder
The band slipping on the bars

media.searchHint: band assisted dip tutorial parallel bars

notes: Marchon: banded dips 5-10 to hit the top of the range. Hitting 4x10 moves to the next lighter band.

technique.setup: Stand on a box between the bars and step up to the top support with straight arms. Lower slowly for 3-5 seconds, then put the feet back down on the box and step up again; never drop off the bars.
cues: Keep the shoulders down away from the ears
Lower for 3-5 seconds to about 90 degrees at the elbow
Keep the elbows pointing back, not out
Step down to the box at the bottom
mistakes: Dropping fast once the elbows pass halfway
Sinking below 90 degrees
Jumping off the bars instead of stepping down
stopIf: Sharp or joint pain in the wrist, elbow or shoulder
Pinching or pain at the front of the shoulder
Unable to control the lowering

name: Dip

technique.setup: Grip the bars and press up to straight arms with the shoulders down. Use a box to get on and off.
cues: Keep the shoulders down away from the ears
Lean slightly forward and lower until the elbows reach about 90 degrees
Keep the elbows pointing back, not out
Press up to straight arms
mistakes: Dropping far below 90 degrees
Shoulders rolling forward and shrugging up at the bottom
Kicking the legs to get up
stopIf: Sharp or joint pain in the wrist, elbow or shoulder
Pinching or pain at the front of the shoulder or collarbone

notes: Journal dose was 6-10 x3-4 on parallel bars.

name: Weighted dip

technique.setup: Hang a dumbbell or plate from a dip belt, or hold a light dumbbell between the feet. Get onto the bars from a box and press up to straight arms.
cues: Keep the shoulders down away from the ears
Lower under control until the elbows reach about 90 degrees
Keep the elbows pointing back, not out
Press up to straight arms without swinging the weight
mistakes: Adding weight before 3x8 bodyweight dips are solid
Going deeper than 90 degrees under load
Letting the weight swing
stopIf: Sharp or joint pain in the wrist, elbow or shoulder
Pinching or pain at the front of the shoulder or collarbone

notes: Journal doses were 5x5, 8x3 and 8-10 x4. Hitting the top of the range means the next weight up. A dip belt is not in the equipment list, so dumbbell stands in.

technique.setup: Sit on an upright bench with the back supported and a dumbbell in each hand at shoulder height, palms forward or facing each other. Feet flat on the floor.
cues: Brace the core and keep the ribs down
Press the dumbbells up and slightly in until the arms are straight
Keep the forearms vertical under the weights
Lower slowly back to shoulder height
mistakes: Arching the lower back to push the weight up
Flaring the elbows straight out to the sides
Choosing a weight that needs a leg drive or a bounce
stopIf: Sharp or joint pain in the shoulder or elbow
Pinching at the top of the shoulder when the arms go overhead

name: Dumbbell lateral raise

technique.setup: Stand tall with a light dumbbell in each hand at the sides, elbows slightly bent. Lean the chest a little forward.
cues: Raise the arms out to the sides to shoulder height, no higher
Lead with the elbows, thumbs level or slightly down
Keep the shoulders down away from the ears
Lower slowly for 2-3 seconds
mistakes: Swinging the body to lift the weight
Shrugging the shoulders up
Lifting above shoulder height
stopIf: Sharp or joint pain in the shoulder
Pinching at the top of the shoulder

notes: Journal: 12 reps superset with DB chest press, x3. A band version works too (stand on the band) but has no id of its own yet.

name: Band triceps pressdown

technique.setup: Anchor the band high in a door and face it, holding the band with both hands at chest height. Pin the elbows to the sides.
cues: Keep the elbows pinned to the ribs
Push the hands down until the arms are straight
Keep the shoulders down and the chest tall
Return slowly to chest height
mistakes: Elbows drifting forward and away from the body
Leaning over the hands to push with body weight
Letting the band snap back up
stopIf: Sharp or joint pain in the elbow
A band that is frayed or a door that is not shut

media.searchHint: resistance band tricep pushdown door anchor form

notes: Shoulder-friendly triceps work; the default shoulder-niggle swap for dips and push-ups.
